root_cause.text: In btrfs, check_removing_space_info() incorrectly freed sub-group btrfs_space_info objects with kfree() even though create_space_info_sub_group() had registered their embedded kobjects via kobject_init_and_add(), so the required kobject_put()-based sysfs teardown never happened and kobj->name leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes check_removing_space_info() in fs/btrfs/block-group.c from kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]) to btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]); the CVE/commit message explicitly states these sub_group elements are created through btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type() calling kobject_init_and_add(), and that without btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(), kobject_put() is not called and the associated kobj->name objects are leaked.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In btrfs, check_removing_space_info() incorrectly freed sub-group btrfs_space_info objects with kfree() even though create_space_info_sub_group() had registered their embedded kobjects via kobject_init_and_add(), so the required kobject_put()-based sysfs teardown never happened and kobj->name leaked.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes check_removing_space_info() in fs/btrfs/block-group.c from kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]) to btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]); the CVE/commit message explicitly states these sub_group elements are created through btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type() calling kobject_init_and_add(), and that without btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(), kobject_put() is not called and the associated kobj->name objects are leaked.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the proper space_info removal helper for subgroups so sysfs entries are cleaned up before the subgroup object is destroyed.
intent_record.what: Inside check_removing_space_info(), the code replaces a direct kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]) call with btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]) after the recursive cleanup of each non-NULL sub_group entry, while keeping the subsequent assignment of the pointer to NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, subgroup space_info objects are no longer just freed directly; they are removed through a dedicated helper that can perform the required sysfs teardown and associated cleanup before releasing the object, preventing stale sysfs state and incomplete destruction of the space_info subgroup.

grouping_result.intent: Use the proper space_info removal helper for subgroups so sysfs entries are cleaned up before the subgroup object is destroyed.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the root cause by replacing raw destruction of subgroup space_info objects with the proper removal helper, ensuring kobject/sysfs teardown occurs before the object is freed and preventing the kobj->name leak.

candidates.rationale: This directly frees a sub-group btrfs_space_info that had an embedded kobject registered through kobject_init_and_add(), bypassing the required kobject_put()-driven teardown and causing the sysfs kobject name leak.

This call is part of the faulty removal sequence for sub-group space_info objects: after this check, the code proceeds to free the object directly instead of using the proper removal helper that would release the embedded kobject and sysfs state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This directly frees a sub-group btrfs_space_info object whose embedded kobject had been registered earlier. Freeing it with kfree() bypasses the required kobject_put()-based teardown, so sysfs cleanup does not occur and the kobject name leaks.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the exact removal path for sub-group space_info objects. In the newly added block inside check_removing_space_info(), the code iterates over children and does: `check_removing_space_info(space_info->sub_group[i]);` followed by `kfree(space_info->sub_group[i]);` and then `space_info->sub_group[i] = NULL;`. According to the stated root cause, sub-group `btrfs_space_info` objects have embedded kobjects registered via `kobject_init_and_add()`, so they must be released through `kobject_put()`/proper sysfs teardown rather than direct `kfree()`. The presence of direct `kfree()` on `space_info->sub_group[i]` is therefore the vulnerable construct. There is no indication here of any `kobject_put()`, sysfs cleanup, or equivalent release helper, so the fix is not present.

commit 1cfdbe0d53b27b4b4a4f4cf2a4e430bc65ba2ba5
Author: Naohiro Aota <naohiro.aota@wdc.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 23 11:43:45 2025 +0900

    btrfs: factor out check_removing_space_info() from btrfs_free_block_groups()
    
    Factor out check_removing_space_info() from btrfs_free_block_groups(). It
    sanity checks a to-be-removed space_info. There is no functional change.
    
    Reviewed-by: Johannes Thumshirn <johannes.thumshirn@wdc.com>
    Signed-off-by: Naohiro Aota <naohiro.aota@wdc.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code is sufficient because it includes the full newly factored helper `check_removing_space_info()` and the relevant call site in `btrfs_free_block_groups()`. The vulnerability root cause is freeing a sub-group `btrfs_space_info` with `kfree()` instead of doing proper kobject teardown via `kobject_put()`, after `create_space_info_sub_group()` had used `kobject_init_and_add()`. In this snippet, `check_removing_space_info()` only performs sanity checks: it warns on `bytes_pinned`, `bytes_may_use`, `bytes_reserved`, and `reclaim_size`, and may call `btrfs_dump_space_info()`. At the call site, the code does `check_removing_space_info(space_info); list_del(&space_info->list); btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info);`. There is no `kfree(space_info)` here, and no kobject release logic in this helper. Therefore the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this function. At the same time, this function does not itself show the fix for the specific bug either, because there is no visible `kobject_put()`-based teardown logic here; it only calls `btrfs_sysfs_remove_space_info(space_info)`, whose internals are not shown. So for this function: the vulnerable `kfree()` misuse is absent (`has_bug=false`), and the fix is also not explicitly present in the shown logic (`is_fixed=false`).
